subject: Re: LegacyBank - On-prem / Air-gapped qualification & next steps

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: LegacyBank - On-prem / Air-gapped qualification & next steps

Hi Paul / IT Ops team —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

What we heard
- LegacyBank requires a fully air-gapped, on-prem deployment for model inference for the Fraud Ops workload (no direct internet egress).
- Primary constraints: offline upgrade process, hardware certification (existing racks + spare capacity), and verification of cryptographic signing for binaries/artifacts.
- Target latency/throughput: ~200 qps for short form inference (avg 256 tokens), burst to 600 qps during peak windows.

Options we discussed
- Hosted API: fastest to prod but not allowed due to data residency / egress policies.
- Dedicated: private, single-tenant in cloud — may still not satisfy air-gap requirement.
- Private (on-prem, air-gapped): primary path forward given constraints; requires schedule for hardware validation and ops dry-run.

Action items / next steps
1) Paul: please share the initial hardware baseline and network isolation diagram (we discussed rack/u positions and switch model). You mentioned you could send a baseline today.
2) Redwood (Rishi + me): we’ll put together an offline upgrade/runbook and a minimal validated HW spec (attached a draft spec and network diagram for reference).
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with our SEs to walk through the offline upgrade flow and signing/verifications — propose 60–90 minutes.

Attachments: network_diagram_v2.pdf (draft), hw_spec_sheet.xlsx (baseline), redwood_onprem_requirements.docx (what we’ll need for an air-gapped deploy).

Available times for the deep-dive: Tue 3/3 10–12 PT, Wed 3/4 14–17 PT, or Fri 3/6 09–11 PT. Please let us know what works.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

We can do the deep-dive on Wed 3/4 15:00 PT — that works for our SE/IT leads. Also cc'd procurement so they can schedule procurement windows on our end.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-03-03T15:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: LegacyBank - On-prem / Air-gapped qualification & next steps

Marissa —

Saw Paul’s note and baseline. High level thoughts before the deep-dive: 

- OS lockdown: we support hardened RHEL variants; we validate on commonly used kernel / glibc combos. We’ll need exact build IDs for the air-gapped validation run.
- Offline upgrades: standard approach we use for air-gapped installs is a signed tarball + detached signature (ed25519) + checksums; vendor provides media (USB or internal repo). We can provide a verification tool that runs locally (no outbound calls).
- Hardware: the baseline looks like 4 x A100 / 80GB per inference cluster node — that will meet the QPS target with our model quantization profile, but we should validate memory footprint on a 256-token tail. If they can provide one test node with SSH (on pre-approved subnetwork) we can run a smoke validation.

I’ll join the Wed 3/4 deep-dive. I can prepare an offline upgrade playbook and a checklist for chain-of-custody items. I recommend we present two options during the call: 
A) Fully air-gapped: customer is responsible for hardware, media handoff, and applying upgrades per our runbook. Redwood provides signed artifacts and a local verification CLI.
B) Semi-managed private: Redwood handles packaging and provides a technician on site for upgrades (still no internet egress) — higher cost but lowers operational burden.

If you want, I can draft the playbook and bring to the call.

—Rishi
Staff Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@legacybank.com>, IT Ops <itops@legacybank.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-05T08:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: LegacyBank - On-prem / Air-gapped qualification & next steps

Paul —

Appreciate the baseline. Quick answers inline and a proposed ask for the deep-dive.

- OS compatibility: we support hardened RHEL builds. For the validation run we’ll need the exact kernel and rpm manifest for the node(s) you want us to test against. Rishi will validate locally; no outbound network calls required.
- Offline upgrades & signing: Redwood provides an offline upgrade package as a signed tarball (ed25519) plus SHA512 checksums. We produce a signed manifest and a small verification binary (static) that your team runs prior to install. For chain of custody, we can include a simple checklist template and require signature stamps on the media handoff.
- Hardware recs: for the QPS you specified, our recommended starting point is 4 x NVIDIA A100 80GB GPUs per cluster node, NVLink enabled, 1.6TB system RAM per node. See attached hw_spec_sheet.xlsx for full details. If rack power is constrained, we can propose an alternate config with more nodes + smaller GPUs; we can run a perf projection during the DEEP-dive.

Proposed deep-dive agenda (60–90m)
1) Introductions & objective check (5m)
2) Walkthrough of offline upgrade flow + verification (20m)
3) Hardware validation & perf projections (20m)
4) Chain of custody / signing + procurement checklist (10m)
5) Q/A + next steps (5–15m)

We’ll bring a draft playbook and the offline verification tool to demo on a test node. Confirmed time: Wed 3/4 15:00 PT works for Rishi and Vivek. Can you confirm the attendee list on your side and whether we should include security?

Thanks — attached: hw_spec_sheet.xlsx, redwood_onprem_requirements.docx, network_diagram_v2.pdf

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Rishi —

Thanks for the detail and the attachments. Wed 3/4 15:00 PT went well — appreciate the walk-through. A few follow ups on our side: 

- Procurement timeline: procurement@legacybank.com is targeting PO approval by end of April; can you provide an itemized BOM and non-cancelable lead times for hardware we recommend?
- Security artifacts: security@legacybank.com will need SOC 2 Type II evidence and your signed artifact process documented. Can you attach the SOC2 attestation and the offline upgrade playbook after you incorporate the items we discussed?
- On-site ops: we like the semi-managed option for the first 90 days to mitigate risk. Can Redwood provide a SOW and pricing for an on-site technician for the initial upgrade window?

Attaching: procurement contact and a rough procurement calendar. Will confirm rack power and exact node build next week.

If you can send the updated playbook, SOC2 attestation, BOM and SOW by next Wed 3/15 that would be ideal for our procurement review.

Best,
Paul
